alate: Alate head brownish, labrum brown, anteclypeus and antennae pale brown, compound eyes reddish brown, ocelli pale, antennal spots light brown; pronotum and sternites both paler than the head capsule, femora and tibiae pale brown, wings brown and slightly paler than the head capsule, sparsely haired. Head nearly circular and slightly long, the compound eyes not very round but semicircularly projecting, their long diameter about 1.5 times the distance to the lower margin of the head capsule; ocelli on the inner side of the compound eyes, raised in the middle; a single elongate-oval antennal spot on the inner side of each antennal socket, smaller than the ocelli and slightly raised in the middle. The Y-shaped suture runs obliquely from the middle of the dorsum of the head to the ocelli, the median suture extremely indistinct; the middle of the posterior margin of the head sometimes with a longitudinal suture reaching one-third of the way up the dorsum. Antennae with 15–16 segments, the second and third equal in length. Labrum flat and square, slightly raised on the dorsum, clypeus nearly a flat trapezoid. Pronotum wider than the head capsule (excluding the compound eyes), about twice as wide as long, the anterior margin arcuately concave with a shallow median notch, the lateral margins curved backwards in an arc, the middle of the posterior margin slightly concave. Wings narrow and long, extending beyond the end of the abdomen and about as long as the abdomen, the wing membrane densely covered with small warts; the radius reaching only a quarter of the wing length, the radius sector parallel with the media as far as the anterior corner of the wing, the radius sector unbranched.
